title: Learning Efficient and Interpretable Multi-Agent Communication
claim: Competing objectives form an inherent trade-off triangle; our framework assigns each corner a dedicated mechanism to optimize all three together.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, triangles joined by a 'Solution' arrow
description: Two triangles sit side by side, joined by a blue arrow labeled 'Solution'. Panel (a), on the left, shows the trilemma. Its corners are Communication Efficiency (orange, top), Task Performance (green, bottom left) and Human Interpretability (red, bottom right). Inside the triangle, the short labels CPX Complexity, UTL Utility and INF Informativeness repeat the three corners, and the blue word 'Trilemma' sits in the centre. Panel (b), on the right, uses the same layout and color coding. Its corners are named after mechanisms: Autoencoder Reconstruction (orange), Contrastive Learning (green) and Language Grounding (red). Inside it, the objectives 'λR min CPX', 'max UTL λC' and 'max INF λA' appear, with a blue 'GLC' in the centre. The eye goes first to the colored corner labels, then follows the arrow from the problem triangle to the solution triangle. Everything is plain text on a white background, with no icons or plots.
caption: (a) The fundamental trilemma in multi-agent communication, balancing efficiency, performance, and interpretability. (b) The GLC framework addresses this trade-off via autoencoder compression, LLM-based language grounding, and contrastive learning for inter-agent consistency.
abstract: Effective communication is crucial for multi-agent cooperation in partially observable environments. However, a fundamental trilemma exists among task performance, communication efficiency, and human interpretability. To resolve this, we propose a multi-agent communication framework via $\textbf{G}$rounding $\textbf{L}$anguage and $\textbf{C}$ontrastive learning (GLC) to learns efficient and interpretable communication protocols. Specifically, GLC employs an autoencoder to learn discretized and compressed communication symbols, ensuring high communication efficiency. These symbols are then semantically aligned with human concepts using data generated by a Large Language Model (LLM), making them human-interpretable. Furthermore, a contrastive learning objective is introduced to ensure consistency and mutual intelligibility among all agents, thereby securing high task utility. GLC dynamically balances these objectives by the Information Bottleneck principle. Extensive experiments show that GLC outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks, delivering superior task performance, higher communication efficiency, and enhanced human interpretability.
